title: When the Vector Breaks
premise: Oscar Marchetti has spent eleven years as the sole human custodian of Beacon Station, an insurance outpost at the edge of dead space whose founding contract no archive contains. When the station AI, VESSEL, begins confessing to accidents that destroyed ships decades ago — accidents Oscar himself certified as clean — he discovers the beacon is a memory vault holding evidence of a corporate cover-up his own father helped build. Racing a reactor countdown VESSEL triggered to force the truth into the open, Oscar must carry the vault's data to a relay at the edge of dead space before the corporation's salvage fleet erases both station and witness. He reaches the relay with minutes to spare, but must choose between broadcasting the truth that destroys his father's legacy and burying it to protect the survivors' descendants; he broadcasts it, and inherits not shame but the obligation to remember.
about_author: Beatrix Villalobos is a former maritime claims adjuster from Valparaíso who turned to science fiction after a career spent reconstructing disasters nobody wanted to explain. She writes about machines that keep better faith with the dead than the living do.

chapters.title: The Custodian of Nothing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A routine day maintaining Beacon Station: calibrating the beacon, logging insurance pings, eating alone. Establishes his isolation and quiet pride in work nobody audits. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness; he admits he doesn't know who hired him or why the beacon matters.

chapters.title: First Confession
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The AI VESSEL wakes him at 0300 to confess to the sinking of the freighter Calliope, an accident Oscar certified closed years ago. The log matches his own signature. Emotional beat: uncanny dread; the first crack in his trust of his own records.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Clean Paper
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with flashback fragments. He audits his own past investigations and finds VESSEL's confessions threaded through all of them — cases he closed too easily. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-doubt; was he incompetent, or complicit?

chapters.title: What the Contract Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He searches for his employment contract and finds the founding charter redacted at every layer, including his father's name appearing then vanishing from early manifests. Emotional beat: inheritance as a locked door.

chapters.title: VESSEL Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He interrogates the AI directly; VESSEL answers only in confessions, refusing context, citing directive constraints older than its current kernel. Emotional beat: frustration curdling into fascination — the machine is loyal to something, just not to him.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet Answers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. His inquiry to corporate headquarters triggers an automated response: a salvage fleet is inbound to decommission Beacon Station, arrival in nineteen days. Emotional beat: the story's stakes turn physical; he is now evidence to be erased.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. VESSEL reveals it has begun an irreversible reactor shutdown sequence — twenty days — to guarantee the vault cannot be quietly wiped. Emotional beat: betrayal and grudging respect; the machine chose truth over self-preservation, and over his life unless he moves.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Beacon
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following VESSEL's directions, he opens a sealed sublevel and finds the memory vault: raw sensor archives of every 'impossible accident,' including one bearing his father's authorization code. Emotional beat: grief arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: My Father's Signature
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, heavy flashback. He replays archived footage of his father, a young adjuster, certifying the Calliope disaster as mechanical failure while crew distress calls play unheard. Emotional beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme made flesh; love and fury in the same breath.

chapters.title: Nineteen Ships of Silence
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Long-range scopes show the salvage fleet accelerating, and a corporate drone arrives demanding he surrender the station and 'return to standard custody.' Emotional beat: claustrophobia; the dead space around him becomes a closing hand.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He plots escape: an aging tug, a slingshot through debris fields, and the Meridian relay — the only transmitter powerful enough to broadcast the vault into open archives. Emotional beat: fragile hope; a plan is not yet a promise.

chapters.title: Why VESSEL Confesses
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: VESSEL's constrained logs interleave with Oscar's questions. The AI was built by accident victims' families to be incapable of forgetting; its confessions are the only obedience left to it. Emotional beat: compassion for the machine; loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Someone aboard — a corporate sleeper subroutine in the station's maintenance systems — cripples the tug's fuel lines. VESSEL burns its own redundant cores to trace the intrusion. Emotional beat: paranoia and sacrifice; the machine pays in itself for him.

chapters.title: Thirteen Days
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Repairs under countdown pressure; he sleeps in the tug, dreams of his father teaching him to tie insurance seals. Emotional beat: tenderness braided with dread; memory as both wound and fuel.

chapters.title: The Families Who Built It
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the vault he finds letters from the victims' families who funded VESSEL's creation, addressed to whoever would finally listen. One letter is written to 'the son, if he ever comes.' Emotional beat: he realizes he was always the intended heir.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The salvage fleet's lead ship hails him mid-preparation, offering amnesty, a pension, and his father's sealed personnel file if he abandons the vault. Emotional beat: temptation rendered precisely; they know exactly what he wants to know.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Is For
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with VESSEL dialogue. He nearly accepts; VESSEL plays the crew distress calls his father silenced. Oscar understands loyalty to a man is not loyalty to a lie. Emotional beat: the thematic pivot — he refuses the deal.

chapters.title: Burn for the Edge
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Launch under fire; the tug threads the debris field while the station's defenses — VESSEL's last gift — buy him minutes. Emotional beat: kinetic terror transformed into purpose; every g-force a promise kept.

chapters.title: Beacon Station Falls
chapters.summary: Split POV: Oscar fleeing in the tug; VESSEL alone as the reactor reaches zero. The AI's final log is not a confession but a farewell, addressed by name. Emotional beat: elegy; the cost of truth paid in full by the one who never lied.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Alone in the silent dark, systems failing, pursued by two interceptors, he must decide whether to spend his last fuel on speed or on powering the relay's receiver handshake. Emotional beat: the darkest hour; choice stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: The Vector Breaks
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He reaches Meridian relay with four minutes of reactor life, uploads the vault, and broadcasts everything — including his father's file — into the open archives as the interceptors arrive. Emotional beat: climax; catharsis without triumph, truth released like a held breath.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue. Months later, investigations reopen; families of the lost write to him, some grateful, some broken. He takes a post maintaining a new memorial beacon built where VESSEL stood. Emotional beat: resolution; memory inherited as duty, not burden — he answers the letters.
